title: The rank of a matrix is unchanged by field extension
statement:
Let $K$ and $L$ be fields [def-weil-field] with $K$ a subfield of $L$ (more generally, let $\iota:K\to L$ be a ring homomorphism of fields, necessarily injective, and view a matrix with entries in $K$ as a matrix with entries in $L$ by applying $\iota$ to every entry). Let $m,n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and let $A=(a_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq m,\ 1\leq j\leq n}$ be an $m\times n$ matrix with entries in $K$. For a field $F$ containing $K$, the rank of $A$ over $F$, written $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)$, is the dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] of the $F$-linear span in $F^n$ of the $m$ rows of $A$; this span is a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], spanned by at most $m$ vectors, so $\operatorname{rank}_F(A)\leq\min(m,n)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{rank}_L(A)=\operatorname{rank}_K(A).
$$

Equivalently, a family of rows of $A$ is linearly independent over $L$ if and only if it is linearly independent over $K$.

None of the three writes the linear algebra out.

proof.text: Use `Matrix.le_rank_map_iff` to characterize each rank bound by a nonvanishing minor. For the identity homomorphism, this gives the corresponding characterization of `r ≤ A.rank`. Since a field ring homomorphism is injective, a minor determinant is nonzero iff its image is nonzero, proving `r ≤ (A.map ι).rank ↔ r ≤ A.rank`; antisymmetry yields rank equality. For the row-family clause, identify `(A.map ι).row i` with `ι ∘ A.row i` and apply Mathlib `linearIndependent_algebraMap_comp_iff` using the algebra structure induced by `ι`.
